opening.argument: Judge, the description does more than invite viewers to watch coding. It points them from the clips to a named bounty program and a separate way to collaborate. A bounty is ordinarily an opportunity to receive payment for completing work, so placing that pathway beside a technical demonstration can function as a reward-linked invitation to act. The description does not state the terms of any bounty, but that omission is precisely why the linked opportunity deserves scrutiny rather than being treated as mere background information.

rebuttal.rebuttal: The live-coding quotes establish what the streamer is doing during the clips; they do not account for the calls to action added in the description. Likewise, the absence of an investment or credential request does not answer whether the named bounty pathway uses the demonstration to attract participants. The defense addresses subscriptions but leaves that distinct invitation largely unexplained.
